stem: A health department reports the case-fatality rate for an infectious disease. Which of the following does this measure express?

options.label: A
options.text: Deaths from the disease per total population at risk
options.misconception: Uses the whole population as denominator, which gives the cause-specific mortality rate.
options.explanation: Deaths from a disease divided by the whole population at risk is the cause-specific mortality rate; its denominator is the population, not the cases.

options.label: B
options.text: New cases of the disease per population over a period
options.misconception: Confuses deaths among cases with incidence of new cases.
options.explanation: New cases per population over a period is incidence, which counts disease occurrence rather than deaths among cases.

options.label: C
options.text: Proportion of the population that has the disease now
options.misconception: Confuses a measure of fatality with prevalence of existing disease.
options.explanation: The share of a population that currently has a disease is prevalence, which says nothing about how many cases die.

options.label: D
options.text: Proportion of people with the disease who die of it
options.misconception: None — case-fatality divides deaths from the condition by the number of cases.
options.explanation: CDC defines the case-fatality rate as the proportion of persons with a particular condition (cases) who die from that condition.

options.label: E
options.text: Deaths from all causes per total population per year
options.misconception: Confuses case-fatality with the crude (all-cause) mortality rate.
options.explanation: Deaths from all causes per total population per year is the crude mortality rate, which uses the whole population as its denominator.

context: Learning objective: The case-fatality rate is the proportion of persons with a condition who die from that condition.
